Plan 276-07 RULED NOT to extend the sibling-writes discount to the WEAK tier specifically so this real, undetected write stays visible rather than being cleared by 'a sibling writes' reasoning. dispositions.reason: tool-router.cjs:1231's intelligence description ('Run intelligence operations: find connections, grade ventures, build thesis, research.') carries a WEAK claim ('build') that extractClaims attaches per-command to every named vocabulary member in the sentence, including research. Newly surfaced by plan 276-07 Task 2's own B-4 includes()-dispatch fix: before that fix, EUREKA_COMPUTE_COMMANDS.includes(command)'s branch body was NOT recognized as consumed, so it stayed part of sharedBodyText and leaked into EVERY command's effectiveText -- including research's -- making research falsely resolve WRITES via a write primitive that belongs to a DIFFERENT command's body. After the fix isolates that body into its own branch, research correctly resolves NO_WRITE and the pre-existing WEAK claim becomes visible. eureka-run/eureka-status/eureka-report are the tool's real writing siblings. Plan 276-07's WEAK-tier sibling-writes ruling (classifyBranch's WEAK-TIER SIBLING-WRITES RULING comment) applies identically here: NOT extended, so this MEDIUM stays permanently visible rather than being cleared by 'a sibling writes' reasoning. Per D-276-2 this is a closed finding, not unfinished work.
